cases.title: Docker Recreate → 容器重建后 Identity/Revision/Journal/Cache 不丢
cases.canonical_before: PARTIAL (attempt04 只覆盖 Identity/Revision/Cache；Journal 需显式采纳 attempt02；Compose 形态重建与 B 恢复后 UI 读回缺失)

covered_dimensions.layer: real docker compose force-recreate + real agent process + named volume + hub api + browser UI
description: Compose form node B (hostname qa-g4-74acdeb973df-compose, deployment_mode=docker, agent binary sha256 d55dc5cd… from the pinned image sha256:ecd4dd9f…) enrolled on repair :18080 and reported online/synced.

Recreate #1 = `docker compose up -d --force-recreate`: container id changed 96cc0c17899f… → 518553dd3235…, the named volume (and therefore the state DB dev/inode) survived, agent process pid changed (183524), agent exe sha256 = d55dc5cd… and the live agent FD and the container-view DB resolve to the same inode as the host volume DB.
Identity preserved: agent identity table identical before/after; Hub node id/agent_id unchanged.
Revision preserved/monotonic: sync_state.global_revision 3610 → 3610 and every hub object matched per revision+sha256.

Journal preserved: the local executions table (the agent execution journal) kept exactly the same row set before/after each recreate (no row lost, none duplicated, statuses SUCCESS / exit_code 0 / stdout marker / synced=1).
Cache preserved: the content-addressed artifact cache kept the same row (sha256 3a5918555a8a7ab2…) and the same physical file (same dev/inode/size/sha256 and same container-view directory listing).

covered_dimensions.layer: real `docker compose down` (volume kept) + `docker compose up -d` + real re-execution
description: Recreate #2 = compose down → container absent / volume and owned network present → two hub-side changes while the agent was offline → compose up -d: new container id 85ab205b3b91…, same volume, agent reconnected and returned online/synced.

After recovery the four dimensions were re-verified (identity identical, revision caught up to the new hub watermark, journal row set unchanged, cache row + physical file identical), and the post-recovery Desired State was applied: owned script-2/task-2 became present locally with the exact hub revision.
A real execution after recovery (run2 = fe8c480f-7e5d-4981-a477-2d72bb3da210) succeeded with the marker stdout, so the recovered agent is functionally live, not merely reconnected.

covered_dimensions.layer: browser UI (own session qa-g4-74acdeb973df-ui) on the repair console
description: UI readback before the recreates (ui1) and after them (ui2): node detail page shows 节点 ID / Agent ID (identity), 全局修订号 r<revision> matching the agent DB value, 同步状态 已同步, 部署模式 docker, 执行 section with the owned task and 成功 status (journal readback) and 托管应用 section listing the owned application.
The agent-side artifact cache has no dedicated UI surface (documented); the UI shows the managed application and the cache itself was verified host/container-side.

Screenshots: evidence/ui1-node-detail.png, evidence/ui1-executions.png, evidence/ui1-applications.png, evidence/ui2-node-detail.png, evidence/ui2-executions.png, evidence/ui2-applications.png, evidence/ui2-artifacts.png.
SYS-12 attempt02 (b9e47f16deb9) Journal evidence is explicitly adopted: execution_journal_status=SUCCESS, exit_code=0, rows_unchanged_across_a_b=true.

This batch adds the same Journal dimension on the Compose form: local execution journal rows unchanged across three container recreates (4 rows, all SUCCESS/exit 0/synced) plus a real post-recovery execution.

remaining_or_limitations: The pinned image carries the old agent build (agent_version dddee4f0-e2e-repair-20261004, binary sha256 d55dc5cd…), exactly as in the reused SYS-12 evidence; running the fixed (cr1) agent inside the Docker form is out of this authorization scope (checklist G4 note) and was not attempted.

No application deploy execution was run on the Docker node: the pinned agent reports application_deploy=false (Hub capability list) — the cache dimension was exercised through the real artifact prefetch of an assigned owned application, which is the cache write path itself.

The shared repair authority had a concurrent batch (qa-g6-1fdba63d-*) creating/deleting its own fixtures in the same window; it also triggered one extra manual execution of the owned task (see harness_notes). No case check depended on a shared counter, so the results are unaffected.

cases.title: Docker Agent Recreate；恢复后幂等、持久化、Desired State 与实际状态一致
cases.canonical_before: PARTIAL (仅持久化子维度可复用；幂等与 Desired State 一致性未覆盖，含 attempt02 desired 1573 vs 本地 1575 的未解释差异)

covered_dimensions.layer: real re-execution + repeated syncs + hub api + agent sqlite
description: Three container recreates (force-recreate, down/up, and the earlier harness restart cycle) each created zero new executions and zero duplicate journal/object rows; the row uniqueness check over scripts/tasks/applications/executions/artifacts held (distinct ids == row count).

Two extra hub-side updates of the owned script-2 (revision 2 → 3) forced two more real sync cycles: no duplicate local rows, no new execution, script-2 local revision tracked the hub revision exactly, and the applied revision followed the hub watermark.

Re-running the owned task produced exactly one new execution (run2 = fe8c480f-7e5d-4981-a477-2d72bb3da210, SUCCESS, marker stdout); the earlier execution f5249cb8-8c7e-496f-88ea-f384eab28621 kept its terminal row unchanged; all local journal rows ended with synced=1 (exactly-once reconciliation to the Hub).

covered_dimensions.layer: hub Desired State vs agent local rows (per object) + hub reconciliation verdict
description: Object-level reconciliation after recovery: for script, script-2, task, task-2 and the owned application the Hub revision equals the local revision and the script content sha256 matches exactly (5 objects, all match=true).

The Hub's own reconciliation verdict was used as the convergence gate: the node row reported sync_status=synced with global_revision equal to the agent local applied revision after each recreate/recovery cycle (heartbeat/SYNC_ACK convergence waited explicitly).
Monotonicity: the agent applied revision never regressed and never exceeded the Hub watermark.

covered_dimensions.layer: fault window (agent stopped) + 2 hub changes + recovery
description: While the agent was stopped the hub watermark advanced by exactly the two owned changes (script-2 and task-2; changelog rows 3611, 3612) while the agent local revision stayed frozen; after restart the agent applied the new watermark, created no duplicate state and re-synced the Desired State exactly once.

covered_dimensions.layer: watermark accounting (hub revision_sequence + node rows + agent local)
description: Reproduced deterministically and explained: hub-side sample = node row 3610 (agent stopped), hub watermark while down = 3612, agent-side read after recovery = 3612 — a delta of 2 equal to the two owned changes that landed in between.

Semantics (source-verified + measured): hub revision_sequence is a single monotonic watermark advanced by every hub-side object change; the agent local value is the watermark delivered in its last SYNC response; the hub node row is the value the agent reports back (SYNC_ACK immediately, heartbeat ≤30s, revision_check 45s). Therefore attempt02 1573 vs 1575 is a sampling-order artifact: the agent value being 2 higher means it had already applied a newer watermark (no state loss, no unapplied Desired State), and object-level revision+sha equality is the real consistency criterion (verified here).

covered_dimensions.layer: reused persistence dimension re-verified on the Compose form
description: Identity/Revision/Journal/Cache persistence re-verified on the Compose form with the same pinned image as the reused SYS-12 evidence (see E2E-18 dimensions); DB dev/inode identical across recreates because the named volume survives.

remaining_or_limitations: Same pinned-image/old-agent scope note as E2E-18 (Docker form runs the pinned old build).

The idempotency statement is "no duplicate state and no extra execution across the fault window", observed on manual-trigger executions; no schedule-driven duplicate window was exercised here (that is the G2/G3/G6 scope).
Concurrent batch activity on the shared authority is recorded in harness_notes; per-object and per-execution-id checks make the results independent of the shared counter.

retained_history.note: Executions and audit rows cannot be deleted by the product API; counts are registered here. The owned node, application, artifact, tasks and scripts were all deleted with GET-after=404.

harness_notes: Volume copy-up pitfall (real environment behavior): Docker copies the image directory metadata into an EMPTY named volume on first start, which reset the owned volume mount point to root:root 0755 and made the agent exit with `init agent: unable to open database file (14)`. The harness now seeds the volume and re-asserts 65534:65534 0700 after compose up (see state.json volume_perm_checks); the running container and all case evidence use the corrected ownership. This is a harness/environment note, not a product defect claim for these two cases.

The pinned image loads tag-less (`<none>:<none>`, digest-pinned); plain `docker images` hides it while `docker images -a` / `docker image inspect <digest>` show it. Cleanup verifies absence via the digest.

Concurrent batch activity: qa-g6-1fdba63d-* fixtures were created/deleted on the same authority during this window, and one extra manual execution of the owned task (f1f6d07b-3815-40cb-8b61-4a71623a9577 at 2026-10-17T04:08:05Z, audit: execute task 36b3dcd2 one second after a login) was not initiated by this harness; all batches share the same admin identity, so the actor cannot be attributed from audit alone. Impact: none on the case checks (set/per-object based, baselines re-captured per phase); the execution is registered as retained history.

Credential hygiene: the UI evidence originally contained the operator username rendered in the console header; it was scrubbed to <operator-username-redacted> and the whole batch directory re-scanned for the credentials file values (result CLEAN). Password and registration token never appeared in any evidence, argv, or stdout.
The owned task/execution history plus audit rows remain on the shared authority by design (no delete API); the node/objects were removed with GET-after 404 records in final-cleanup-oracle.json.
